title: Four formations
summary: Singleback, I-Form, Shotgun, and Spread, and when a coach picks each one.

steps.text: A formation is where the 11 players stand before the snap. Coaches pick formations to match the play. Here is Singleback: the quarterback under center with one running back behind him. Balanced. Good for a run or a pass.
I-Form puts a fullback between the quarterback and the running back, in a straight line like the letter I. The fullback is an extra blocker. This is a power formation for running the ball.
In Shotgun the quarterback stands about 5 yards behind the center and catches the snap in the air. He can see the whole field and does not have to back up before throwing. Great for passing.
Spread puts four receivers out wide and the quarterback in the shotgun. The defense has to spread out to cover everyone, which leaves fewer defenders in the middle.

A quick way to tell them apart: count the backs and count the receivers. One back under center is Singleback. Two backs in a line is I-Form. Quarterback 5 yards back is Shotgun. Four receivers wide is Spread.

quiz.prompt: Which formation has the quarterback, a fullback, and a running back in a straight line?
quiz.explanation: Three players in a line like the letter I is the I-Form.

quiz.prompt: In Shotgun, how far back does the quarterback stand?
quiz.explanation: About 5 yards. He catches the snap in the air.
The fullback stands between the quarterback and the running back.

quiz.prompt: A coach wants four receivers running routes to stretch the defense. Which formation?
quiz.explanation: Spread puts four receivers wide so the defense has to cover the whole field.

quiz.prompt: Which formation is best known as a power running formation?
quiz.explanation: I-Form adds a fullback as an extra blocker in front of the runner.
